LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we read different types of materials? 2. What kind of materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning,
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information,
3. realise the importance of independent reading in a variety of contexts for enjoyment. The learner is guided to: electronic materials related to the theme such as narratives, poems and graded readers, where they meet on a regular basis to read extensively, read in pairs or groups, reflections on the texts they have read, used in graded readers. read different types of materials? materials do you enjoy reading? do to remember what you read?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
4. Show that you can: read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why should we read different types of materials? 2. What kind of materials do you enjoy reading?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
